title: Wild Bill Davison and the Swiss festival in Bern
summary: Davison brought Leeman to the Bern festival in 1976; they played Geneva and Zurich and Leeman praises his driving trumpet at age 73 and the old Condon drinking days.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Now I'd like to get to Wild Bill -- Wild Bill

Davi son, and I'm trying to get to these people one by one to keep in context with my career, but we don't have time, as I have said several times before, to get into the many jobs that we've done together.

So I'll skip over lightly on some of the things the first London years over the years, ever since my first years with Wild Bill Davison -- in 1976, he was instrumental in bringing me to the Swiss International Jazz Festival held in Bern, Switzerland. We also played Geneva and Zurich, Germany, the group the first two years was Ed Hubble on trombone, Peanuts Hucko on clarinet, Bob Wilbur on clarinet and there goes my mental block -- on soprano saxophone, Bob Wilbur Ralph Sutton on piano and with the Swiss bassist.

Wild Bill lives in Copenhagen, Denmark, and I have joined him and Bern for the last three years. Bill and I have great respect for each other, the other's talent, and he is one of a kind, period. He is a driving trumpet player of great reknown, and not even beginning to slow down at 73 years of age.
Over the past years, the bygone years, we were known to raise a few elbows with Eddie Condon, and with Eddie Condon's prowess as a boozer, the three of us took on all comers.
Bill will be back again this year, and I will be doing concerts with him -- I think I mentioned that before, and

Al Lawson will be going and Eddie Condon's number three nightclub, which is owned by Red Balaban - he was a friend of Condon's, and he had permission from Eddie Condon's' wife to use her name in the present club here in New York.
